glosses: A sudden, intense, loud sound, as made for example by cymbals.

examples.text: The piece ended in a crescendo, building up to a crash of cymbals.
After the lightning came the crash of thunder.

glosses: An automobile, airplane, or other vehicle accident.

examples.text: She broke two bones in her body in a car crash.
Nobody survived the plane crash.

glosses: A malfunction of computer software or hardware which causes it to shut down or become partially or totally inoperable.

examples.text: My computer had a crash so I had to reboot it.

glosses: A sudden large decline of business or the prices of stocks (especially one that causes additional failures).

examples.text: the stock market crash

glosses: A comedown from a drug.
A group of rhinoceroses.

examples.text:
One of my favorites among the terms of groups of creatures is a crash of rhinoceros. I can imagine an African guide saying to his client, “Shoot, dammit, shoot! Here comes the whole bloody crash of rhinoceros!”
[…] Personally, I think I’d just as soon come across a crash of rhinoceros as a knot of toad.

glosses: A sudden decline in any living form's population levels, often leading to extinction.
Quick, fast, intensive, impromptu.

examples.text: crash course
crash diet

glosses: To collide with something destructively; to fall or come down violently.

examples.text: When the car crashed into a house, the driver was heavily injured.
After driving into a tree last week, grandpa's crashed into a deer this morning.

glosses: To cause something to collide with something else, especially when this results in damage.

examples.text: I'm sorry for crashing the bike into a wall. I'll pay for repairs.

glosses: To hit or strike with force.

examples.text: Roy Hodgson's side were dominant and fully merited the lead given to them when Eric Dier crashed a 20-yard free-kick high past keeper Igor Akinfeev with 17 minutes left.

Even the staid New York Times was gushing: “Rising to the glorious heights of his heyday, Babe Ruth, the Sultan of Swat, crashed out three home runs against the Pittsburgh Pirates Saturday afternoon but it was not enough."

glosses: To make a sudden loud noise.

examples.text: Thunder crashed directly overhead.

glosses: Ellipsis of gatecrash.

examples.text: We weren't invited to the party so we decided to crash it.

Friday night I crashed your party
Saturday I said, "I'm sorry"
Sunday came and trashed me out again
"Anyway, sorry about crashing. I know you're doing a sort of 'talk freely about magic' thing, and I don't have any of my own, but..."

glosses: To accelerate a project or a task or its schedule by devoting more resources to it.

examples.text: Using the project plan, the team started to work out different scenarios to crash the schedule and bring the date to the regulatory deadline.

glosses: To make or experience informal temporary living arrangements, especially overnight.

examples.text: Hey dude, can I crash at your pad?

glosses: To give, as a favor.

examples.text: 'I been pissin' blood,' he said, grinning. Then frowning. 'Crash us a tenner, eh?'

glosses: To lie down for a long rest, sleep or nap, as from tiredness or exhaustion.
To experience a period of depression and/or lethargy after a period of euphoria, as after the euphoric effect of a psychotropic drug has dissipated.

examples.text: Falling from cloud nine / Crashing from the high / I'm letting go tonight / Yeah, I'm falling from cloud nine

glosses: To terminate or halt execution due to an exception.

examples.text: If the system crashes again, we'll have it fixed in the computer shop.

glosses: To cause an exception that terminates or halts execution.

examples.text: Double-clicking this icon crashes the desktop.

glosses: To take a sudden and severe turn for the worse; to rapidly and catastrophically deteriorate.

examples.text: And the unvarying lesson of history is that all such balance of power peaces have crashed into new conflicts, as soon as the unstable equilibrium was disturbed, witness the Peace of Westphalia, the Congress of Vienna, and, in our own time, Versailles.
In October 1929, the United States' stock market crashed, at the end of a buoyant decade in its domestic economy.
Despite the quotas determined by fisheries scientists, the Atlantic cod population crashed in the mid-1980s leading to a complete moratorium for fishing the species within Canadian waters.
Nature, propelled by its unidirectional increasing entropic disorder, without the containing Schrodinger and de Broglie λ = h/p waves, would have probably crashed out of existence long ago!
I told him that if his patients got in trouble and started to crash, there are several things that I could do for him.

The analysis presented in Figure 5.2 highlights the importance of technological shocks, which were for example vital in explaining the Information Technology driven bubble of the late 1990s that crashed in 2001.

glosses: To take a subject at higher level without having previously studied it.

examples.text: Joe's crashing Higher Physics, even after I told him it was a bad idea.

glosses: A type of rough linen.

examples.text: The yearly allowance of clothing on this plantation, consisted of two tow-linen shirts—such linen as the coarsest crash towels are made of[…]

Unlocking the door of her bath-room she went inside, and soon emerged, bringing a rug, which she spread upon the floor of the gallery, and two huge hair pillows covered with crash, which she placed against the front of the building.

glosses: To restore to good working order, fix, or improve damaged condition; to mend; to remedy.

examples.text: to repair a house, a road, a shoe, a ship
to repair a shattered fortune
Secret refreſhings, that repair his ſtrength,

glosses: To make amends for, as for an injury, by an equivalent; to indemnify for.

examples.text: to repair a loss or damage
I'll repair the misery thou dost bear.

glosses: The act of repairing something.

examples.text: I took the car to the workshop for repair.
One of the hidden glories of Victorian engineering is proper drains.[…]But out of sight is out of mind. And that[…]means that many old sewers have been neglected and are in dire need of repair.

glosses: The result of repairing something.

examples.text: If you look closely you can see the repair in the paintwork.

glosses: The condition of something, in respect of need for repair.

examples.text: The car was overall in poor repair before the accident. But after the workshop had it for three weeks it was returned in excellent repair. But the other vehicle was beyond repair.
The 1300 class (Nos. 1301-16), one of which was damaged beyond repair in an accident, are Co-Cos, weigh 111 tons and have a top speed of 85 m.p.h.
Thirteen houses were damaged beyond repair, and much of the rest of the town suffered broken windows and lost slates.

glosses: The act of repairing or resorting to a place.

examples.text: our annual repair to the mountains
The king sent a proclamation for their repair to their houses.

glosses: A place to which one goes frequently or habitually; a haunt.

examples.text: There the fierce winds his tender force assail / And beat him downward to his first repair.

glosses: To transfer oneself to another place.

examples.text: to repair to sanctuary for safety
Go, mount the winds, and to the shades repair.
At the hour of half-past five we repaired to our engagement.
At a late hour, after I had been in bed some time, I heard the visitors repair to their chambers:
That finished, I repaired to my room, one flight up, and, after a thorough wash, seated myself, pipe in mouth, at the little window that opened on the Rue Garde.

glosses: To pair again.

examples.text: Please try to repair the two earbuds to each other. Place both earbuds back into the charging case, wait for four seconds, then open it and see if they have been repaired with one another.

glosses: A failure, particularly one which is mechanical in nature.

examples.text: Whenever he was behind the wheel, he would panic at the first sign of a breakdown.

He declared that these drastic steps would undoubtedly inconvenience a good many people, but the alternative was bankruptcy of the Ulster Transport Authority and the breakdown of public transport services.

glosses: A failure, particularly one which is mechanical in nature.

Something, such as a vehicle, that has experienced a mechanical failure.

examples.text: We saw a breakdown by the side of the road.

glosses: Separation of a thing into components; decomposition, fragmentation; (countable) an instance of this.
Detailed categorization, or itemization or listing, of the components of a thing; (countable) an instance of this.

examples.text: Looking at the breakdown of the budget, I see a few items we could cut.

glosses: Separation of a thing into components; decomposition, fragmentation; (countable) an instance of this.

glosses: (Sudden) worsening of physical health or (more commonly) mental stability, resulting in an inability to carry on normal activities; (countable) an instance of this.

examples.text: After so much stress, he suffered a breakdown and simply gave up.

glosses: Injury to a horse's leg causing lameness; (countable) an instance of this.

examples.text: England beat Georgia in their Pool B World Cup match in Dunedin but the stuttering nature of the performance will be of concern to manager Martin Johnson. glosses: An act of splitting logs of wood using a large saw in a sawmill; also, the saw used; or (rare) the building in which the process is carried out.
A part of a piece of music or a song which differs from the other parts in that it features improvisation or is stripped down (for example, played by fewer instruments or a solo performer).

examples.text: And now it's time for a breakdown.

glosses: Synonym of percussion break (“a percussion-focused segment of a song, chosen by a hip-hop DJ to manipulate through cutting, mixing, and other techniques in order to create rhythmic music”).
A section of a song, typical in hardcore music and related styles (such as metalcore, grindcore, and deathcore), characterized by a lower tempo and greater heaviness and intensity of sound.

examples.text: The fired-up foursome [Trial] takes itself very seriously, singing politically charged lyrics, which, in the tradition of Strife and Damnation AD, are strategically placed in the middle of slamming, moshable breakdowns.

glosses: A noisy, rapid, shuffling dance engaged in competitively by a number of individuals or pairs in succession, common among African-Americans from the Southern United States; also, a lively event, chiefly in a rural setting, at which such dancing is done; a hoedown, a shindig.

examples.text: Come, hold on, boys, do n't clear out when the quadrilles are over, for we are going to have a break down to wind up with.

A fiddle, a banjo, and a clarinet—these were the instruments. The trio took their places side by side, and began to play some rattling dance-music, and beat time with their big boots.

glosses: A piece of music played for such a dance, especially a rapid bluegrass tune featuring a five-string banjo.

examples.text: Without a change of countenance, as if he were deaf to her entreaties and threats, he tuned up the banjo, and played a breakdown.

Mama loves you. I left you a good pair of shoes in there on the kitchen table. They shine up easy."
